# brainconn <img src="man/img/logo.png" align="right" alt="" width="180" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/sidchop/brainconn/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/sidchop/brainconn/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

brainconn makes publication-ready plots of brain connectivity data in R, so that visualisation can be part of reproducible analysis scripts:

- `brainconn()`: static 3D renders of brain networks in the style of BrainNet Viewer, as ggplot objects.
- `brainconn3D()`: interactive 3D plots; hover over a node to see its connections, and click it to highlight them.
- `brainconn_matrix()`: connectivity matrices grouped by network, with network borders, smoothing and network-level summaries.
- `brainconn_circle()`: chord diagrams of connectivity within and between networks.
- `brainconn2d()`: 2D plots over a brain image (the `brainconn()` of versions before 1.0.0).

Many commonly used atlases are included (see `list_atlases()`), and you can use your own atlas and your own brain mesh. Rat and macaque brains are included too.

Start with the [Getting started](https://sidchop.github.io/brainconn/articles/brainconn.html) guide, then [A guide to every function](https://sidchop.github.io/brainconn/articles/guide.html) and [Custom atlases and other brains](https://sidchop.github.io/brainconn/articles/other-brains.html).

## Installation

```{r eval = FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("sidchop/brainconn")
```

## Citation

**If you use this package in your research, please cite:**

**Sidhant Chopra, Loïc Labache, Elvisha Dhamala, Edwina R Orchard, Avram Holmes (2023). *A Practical Guide for Generating Reproducible and Programmatic Neuroimaging Visualizations* ApertureNeuro.**

**https://doi.org/10.52294/001c.85104**

## Use

See the [vignette](https://sidchop.github.io/brainconn/articles/brainconn.html) (or `vignette("brainconn")`) for more examples. The main input is a connectivity matrix, `conmat`, whose rows and columns match the regions of an atlas.

### 3D renders

```{r render, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
library(brainconn)
brainconn(atlas = "schaefer300_n7", conmat = example_weighted_undirected,
          view = "ortho", edge.color.weighted = TRUE)
```

### Interactive 3D, with highlighting

```{r, eval = FALSE}
brainconn3D(atlas = "schaefer300_n7", conmat = example_weighted_undirected,
            edge.color.weighted = TRUE, highlight = TRUE)
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "80%"}
knitr::include_graphics("vignettes/figures/brainconn3D-highlight.png")
```

### Connectivity matrices

```{r matrix, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
brainconn_matrix(example_fc_schaefer300, atlas = "schaefer300_n7")
```

### Chord diagrams

```{r chord, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 7}
brainconn_circle(example_fc_schaefer300, atlas = "schaefer300_n7")
```

### Other brains

```{r macaque, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 7}
set.seed(3)
n <- nrow(macaque_atlas)
conmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
conmat[sample(which(upper.tri(conmat)), 50)] <- runif(50, -1, 1)
conmat <- conmat + t(conmat)
brainconn(atlas = macaque_atlas, conmat = conmat, mesh = macaque_mesh, view = "ortho",
          edge.color.weighted = TRUE)
```

### Report bugs or requests

Don't hesitate to ask for support or new features using [GitHub issues](https://github.com/sidchop/brainconn/issues).

### Other R packages you might be interested in

* [ggseg](https://github.com/ggseg/ggseg) & [ggseg3d](https://github.com/ggseg/ggseg3d): plotting tools for brain atlases, in ggplot/plotly
